item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm gonna take you up on that offer, Clef. Aside from what was specifically suggested, I made some other changes:

  • Removed the "preferably" from the last line of the containment procedures — if it's important, they should always wear restraints, and if it's not, then there's no reason to mention them. It's not like the Foundation is prone to running out of ways to keep people's mouths shut.
  • Added sodium to the list of things it's high in, because A) most things we think of as being really unhealthy (especially to the heart) have lots of sodium, at least for processed foods, and B) Too much sodium is also bad for the heart.
  • Amped up the amount of toppings a bit, because when you visualize it, 2 cc of any given condiment is barely enough to cover one patty, more or less three.

I also eyeballed the dinner plate measurements — 18cm is about 7 inches. If anyone has a plate nearby that would give them a better measurement, I'd say defer to them.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
SCP-807 is a salmon-colored ceramic plate, of the standard dimensions for a dinner plate

Please be more specific about it's dimensions.

SCP-807 has the unusual property of

Isn't that a bit redundant? All SCPs have unusual properties, and "anomaly" sounds more professional. Just say what it does ("the object transmutes any food served upon it" etc).

a fatty, cholesterol-laden variation of its original form

The word "fatty" doesn't sound clinical at all.

Once transmuted, the food in question is enhanced in flavor and aroma to preternatural levels, to the point where the desire to consume said food becomes nearly irresistible

This isn't the same as a psychic/memetic compulsion, sure, but it still feels like tacked on danger.

[DATA EXPUNGED: BY ORDER OF O5-5, NO FURTHER EXPERIMENTS ON HIGH-FAT FOODS SHALL BE CARRIED OUT ON SCP-807 DUE TO THE HIGH NUMBER OF CASUALTIES]

This is just too hysterical of a warning for transmuted food. It even specifies which O5 gave the order!

All in all, this isn't that bad, but it needs some fixing. Also, it simply begs for an experiment log. What happens if you put something that isn't food on it? How about the dead body of a small animal, like a rat or a squirrel?

This has potential. No vote for now.
